newsitem.title: USA: U.S. May spot natgas drifts lower, Apr also softer.
newsitem.headline: U.S. May spot natgas drifts lower, Apr also softer.

text.p: U.S. spot natural gas prices for May eroded below last week's levels Monday as ample storage supplies and seasonable weather weakened demand, industry sources said.
May Louisiana Gulf Coast prices at the Henry Hub fell an average of six cents to $2.08-2.10 per million British thermal units (mmBtu), still up about 25 cents from April indices.
Meanwhile, prices at the hub for Tuesday delivery eased by more than 10 cents to about $2.08 as warmer-than-normal weather moved into the region and was expected to continue through week's end.
Similarly in south Texas, May prices lost about four cents to about $2.00-2.02.
Incremental demand may escalate later in the week as some air-conditioning needs surface in western Texas, market sources said.

In the Northeast, where normal to above-normal temperatures are expected most of this week, May New York city-gate prices were still talked in the $2.40s. Prices for Tuesday, which is forecast to be the coolest day of the week, were five to 10 cents softer at $2.35-2.40.
Appalachian prices for next month were quoted at $2.32-2.36 on Columbia and $2.33-2.38 on CNG.
At the Chicago city-gate, May gas traded mostly around $2.17, while prices for Tuesday fell about 10 cents to $2.10-2.13. Detroit city-gate prices were at $2.20-2.32 for May, market sources said.
Elsewhere in the Midcontinent, May prices erased last week's gains to about $1.94-1.96, with Demarcation quoted mostly in the low-to-mid $1.90s.
April prices in the Midcontinent were for the most part in convergence with May in the low-to-mid $1.90s.
Further west, Permian basin prices for May 1 slid five cents to $1.83-1.89, still holding about a 25-cent premium to April 1. San Juan gas traded in the low-to-mid $1.80s.
Swing Permian prices were talked in the mid-to-high $1.80s, about even with May baseload.
At the southern California border, May prices were talked about five cents lower at $1.95-2.00.
Warmer-than-normal temperatures are expected to blanket the Southwest through the week, Weather Services Corp said.
